title: Judge Says White House Cannot Ban Reporters Over Their News
summary:
A federal judge ruled late Tuesday that President Trump cannot keep news reporters out of the White House just because he does not like what they report. The ruling lasts at least until the case goes to a full trial.

Last month, the government took away the White House passes of more than 70 reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico. The three news groups sued.

Judge Timothy J. Kelly said the ban likely broke the reporters' right to free speech. He said it also likely broke their right to a fair warning and a fair chance to object. Both rights are in the U.S. Constitution.

The government said the ban was about keeping the country safe. The judge did not agree. He pointed to the president's own words. He also said Trump's worries about fair news are not necessarily wrong.

A lawyer for the news groups praised the ruling. The White House did not answer right away.
why_it_matters: Free speech protects everyone's right to share and learn the news, including what kids read about their leaders.
